analyst_view.overall: Le Mans are 17th with 7 points, have won one of their last nine games, haven't won in four, and have conceded in nine straight matches. Monaco are seventh but winless in four league games, though they beat Nordsjaelland 2-0 in the Conference League on Thursday; Filipe Luis called that win crucial but admitted his side were slow in the first half and still lacked creativity. Le Mans are without Adil Bourabaa after ankle surgery, and one preview lists no Monaco absentees.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals. Monaco's lack of creativity, which Filipe Luis himself pointed to, and Le Mans missing Bourabaa argue for fewer. But Monaco have conceded in five straight away games and Le Mans have conceded in nine in a row, so we no longer see enough to go below the model.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.0 corners. Monaco should have more of the ball, but they have won fewer corners than expected lately, and nothing in the news moves us away from the model.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.6 cards, which is already high. Le Mans have picked up 18 cards in their last six games and are fighting relegation against a side that will have more of the ball. Bastien Dechepy averages 4.5 cards a game, so we'd sooner go above the model's number than below it.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.2 shots. Monaco take plenty of shots even when they struggle to score, and Le Mans need something at home, so we see no strong reason to move.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.6 shots on target. Filipe Luis said his side lacked creativity on Thursday and were caught offside twice in the second half, and Le Mans are without Bourabaa, so we expect more of the shots to be blocked or off target.
